text:
Both parts of the report are addressed on branch `fix/files-upload-retry` (three commits, all tests green including `-race`).

## Root cause of the retry failure

It wasn't the retry policy — it was body replayability. `Raw.Do` hands upload bodies to `http.NewRequestWithContext`, which only sets `Request.GetBody` (the replay hook) for `*bytes.Buffer`, `*bytes.Reader`, and `*strings.Reader`. For anything else — an `*os.File`, a streamed multipart body — `GetBody` stayed nil, and the retry transport correctly refuses to retry a request whose consumed body it can't resend (`pipedrive/retry.go:130`), so the 429 surfaced immediately. The user's other calls retried fine because JSON bodies are marshaled into a `bytes.Reader`. Note their `RetryAllMethods: true` was never the issue: 429 is retried regardless of method; only the body was the blocker.

## What changed

- **`fix(raw)`** — `Raw.Do` now derives `GetBody` for any body that implements `io.Seeker` (`pipedrive/raw.go`), seeking back to the offset the body had when the request was built. This makes `Files.Add` with an `*os.File` or any seekable multipart body retryable. Non-seekable readers (e.g. `io.Pipe`) keep the safe stream-once behavior, now documented on `Files.Add`/`Update`.
- **`feat(v1)`** — new `Files.Upload(ctx, fileName, content io.Reader, opts...)`, mirroring `CallLogs.AddRecording`. It builds the multipart body via the shared `internal/multipartbody` helper (extended with `NewFileWithFields`), so the body is a buffered `*bytes.Reader` and retries work by construction. Typed options cover the association form fields `POST /files` accepts: `WithUploadFileDealID/PersonID/OrgID/ProductID/ActivityID/LeadID/ProjectID`, plus `WithUploadFileRequestOptions`.
- **`chore(docs)`** — CHANGELOG entries under Unreleased, and a README section explaining which bodies are replayable, with a `Files.Upload` example.
